name: Birmingham Roller
fact: Bred to somersault backwards in the air, sometimes many times in a row, then fly on as if nothing happened.

name: Western European house mouse
fact: Male mice sing ultrasonic courtship songs, too high-pitched for humans to hear.

name: Indian Runner duck
fact: Runs instead of waddling - farmers once walked whole flocks out to the rice paddies to eat pests.

name: Bubble Eye goldfish
fact: Its giant eye bubbles jiggle as it swims, and can pop - then slowly grow back.
credit: Angie Torres from Toronto · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Giant Canada goose
fact: Was thought extinct until a flock was found wintering in a city park in Minnesota.

name: Fancy rat
fact: Laughs (ultrasonically) when tickled, and will chase the hand that does it for more.

name: Polish chicken
fact: Its crest sprouts from a bony dome on its skull and can cover its eyes so much that it startles easily.

name: Common pill woodlouse
fact: Not an insect at all - it's a land crustacean, more closely related to shrimp.

name: Seven-spot ladybird
fact: Oozes bitter, smelly 'reflex blood' from its knees when threatened.
credit: Photographer: Dominik Stodulski Graphic Processing: User:MathKnight · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Canadian nightcrawler
fact: Breathes through its skin, which is why it surfaces when the ground floods.

name: Common housefly
fact: Tastes with its feet.

name: Sebastopol goose
fact: Its feathers curl so much that it looks permanently caught in a gale.

name: English Pouter
fact: Puffs its crop up until it looks like it swallowed a balloon.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
fact: Was bred to herd cattle by nipping their heels - the short legs keep it under the kicks.

name: Nine-banded armadillo
blurb: Species of armadillo native to South America
fact: Almost always gives birth to four identical clones from a single egg.

name: Flemish Giant rabbit
fact: One of the biggest rabbit breeds - some outweigh a small dog.

name: Blobfish
fact: Only looks like a blob out of water - at depth, it looks like a normal fish.

name: Lord Howe Island stick insect
fact: The 'tree lobster' was found again living under a single bush on Ball's Pyramid.

name: Olm
fact: A blind cave salamander that can go a decade without eating.

name: Pink fairy armadillo
fact: The smallest armadillo - pink because blood shows through its shell.

name: Purple frog
fact: Lives buried in the soil of India's Western Ghats and surfaces only for a couple of monsoon weeks to breed - it looks like a deflated purple blob with a pig snout.
credit: Original uploader was Karthickbala at ta.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Eastern cottontail
blurb: Species of rabbit in the genus Sylvilagus
fact: Escapes predators by running in sharp zigzags.

name: Brown garden snail
fact: Can seal itself inside its shell and sleep through months of drought.

name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
fact: Doubles its body weight in fat before crossing the Gulf of Mexico in one go.

name: North American beaver
fact: Its biggest known dam, in Canada's Wood Buffalo park, can be seen from space.
credit: Steve from Washington, DC, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Eastern spotted skunk
fact: Does a full handstand and walks on its front paws at you before spraying.
credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Midwest Region · Public domain

name: European hedgehog
fact: Chews toxic things and lathers the foamy spit onto its spines - nobody's sure why.

name: Florida box turtle
fact: A hinged shell lets it close up completely - a true box.

name: Mexican free-tailed bat
blurb: Species of bat native to the Americas
fact: Clocked at 160 km/h in level flight - possibly the fastest flier outside a dive.

name: Veiled chameleon
fact: Its tongue shoots out from 0 to 97 km/h in a hundredth of a second.

name: Atlantic puffin
fact: Its rough tongue pins fish against spines in its beak, so it can keep catching with a full mouth.

name: Blue-footed booby
fact: Males strut and lift their bright blue feet one at a time to impress females.

name: Black-tailed prairie dog
fact: Its alarm calls encode a predator's species, size, colour and speed.

name: Pygmy hippopotamus
fact: Moo Deng, a baby pygmy hippo in Thailand, became one of the most famous animals online in 2024.

name: Vaquita
fact: The rarest marine mammal on Earth.

name: Yeti crab
fact: The 'yeti crab' farms bacteria on its hairy arms - and may eat them.
credit: Andrew Thurber, Oregon State University · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Dumbo octopus
fact: The deepest-living octopus - it flaps its ear-like fins to 'fly' through the abyss.

name: Superb lyrebird
fact: Copies almost any sound - other birds, car alarms, chainsaws - perfectly.

name: Peacock spider
fact: The peacock spider - a male raises a jewel-coloured fan and dances to win a mate.

name: Immortal jellyfish
blurb: Species of small, biologically immortal jellyfish
fact: The 'immortal jellyfish' can turn back into a juvenile and start its life over.

name: Narwhal
fact: Its 'horn' is a tooth growing out through its lip, packed with millions of nerve endings.

name: Pistol shrimp
blurb: Family of crustacean possessing asymmetrical snapping claws
fact: Its claw snap fires a bubble that briefly gets nearly as hot as the surface of the sun.

name: Saiga antelope
fact: That bulbous nose is a built-in air filter for dusty summers and frozen winters.

name: Shoebill
fact: Looks like a dinosaur, eats lungfish and baby crocodiles, and 'claps' its bill to communicate.

name: West Indian Ocean coelacanth
fact: Thought extinct for 66 million years, until one turned up in a fishing net in 1938.

name: Pug
fact: Bred as lapdogs for Chinese emperors - some were kept in palaces with their own guards.

name: Dachshund
fact: Its loud bark is deliberate - so hunters could hear it underground.

name: Shetland pony
fact: Pound for pound one of the strongest horse breeds - it once hauled coal down mines.

name: Jacob sheep
fact: Rams can grow four or even six horns at once, sticking out in all directions.
credit: David Merrett from Daventry, England · CC BY 2.0

name: Silkie
blurb: Topics referred to by the same term
fact: Marco Polo described a "chicken with fur" - its fluffy feathers have no hooks to zip them flat.

name: Angora rabbit
fact: Its wool is warmer than sheep wool and is gathered by brushing or plucking as it moults.

name: Fainting goat
fact: When startled its muscles lock up and it often tips over - it doesn't actually faint.

name: Alpaca
blurb: Domesticated species of South American camelid
fact: A whole herd uses a few communal dung piles, which makes them easy to house-train.

name: Guinea pig
fact: Not a pig and not from Guinea - excited ones leap straight up in the air, called 'popcorning'.

name: Roborovski dwarf hamster
fact: The smallest hamster species, and one of the fastest for its size.

name: European herring gull
fact: Pecks the red spot on its parent's beak to make it cough up dinner.

name: Banana slug
fact: The second-largest land slug on Earth - its slime numbs the tongues of would-be predators.
credit: Andy.goryachev at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Monarch butterfly
blurb: Milkweed butterfly in the family Nymphalidae
fact: No single butterfly makes the round trip - it takes several generations to get back north.
credit: Photo by and (c)2007 Derek Ramsey (Ram-Man) · GFDL 1.2

name: Common earwig
fact: Despite the myth, it doesn't crawl into ears - but mothers do guard and clean their eggs.

name: Long-bodied cellar spider
fact: Shakes its web so fast it becomes a blur - and happily hunts other spiders.

name: Zebrafish
fact: Can regrow up to a fifth of its heart - which is why scientists study it so closely.

name: Siamese fighting fish
blurb: Species of fish native to Southeast Asia
fact: Males build floating nests of spit bubbles and guard the eggs inside.

name: Brine shrimp (Sea-Monkey)
fact: Their dried eggs can survive years of drought - and even a trip to space - then hatch in water.

name: Cane toad
fact: Brought to Australia to eat beetles; it ignored them and spread across the continent instead.

name: American bullfrog
fact: Eats almost anything it can fit in its mouth - including other bullfrogs, snakes and bats.

name: Common snapping turtle
fact: Can whip its head around astonishingly fast - and can reach back to its own hind legs.
credit: Chuck Homler, Focus On Wildlife · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Red-eared slider
fact: Named for the way it slides off rocks and logs into the water at the first sign of trouble.

name: Leopard gecko
fact: Unlike most geckos it has eyelids and can't climb glass - and blinks at you.

name: Central bearded dragon
fact: Waves one arm in a slow circle to signal submission to bigger dragons.
credit: Photograph: Frank C. Müller, Baden-Baden · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: Anolis carolinensis
fact: Often called the 'American chameleon' - it shifts between green and brown.

name: Eastern chipmunk
fact: Can gather up to 165 acorns a day, stuffing its cheeks to carry them home.

name: Wild turkey
blurb: Species of turkey native to North America
fact: Unlike farm turkeys, wild ones fly well and roost in trees at night.

name: Muscovy duck
fact: It hardly quacks at all - males hiss, and females make a small trilling coo.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Llama
fact: Some farmers use llamas as guards - they chase off foxes and coyotes from sheep flocks.

name: Baudet du Poitou
fact: Its shaggy coat grows into long cords called cadenettes - a status symbol in old France.

name: Mangalica
fact: A pig with a woolly fleece like a sheep - it nearly died out in the 1990s.

name: Kunekune
fact: Small enough to be a pet and grazes on grass, which most pigs cannot live on alone.

name: Belted Galloway
fact: Black at both ends with a white belt round the middle, just like a sandwich biscuit.

name: Valais Blacknose
fact: Black face, black knees and spiralling horns, with a white fleece that looks like a soft toy.

name: Lionhead rabbit
fact: A single dominant gene gives it a woolly mane around its head like a tiny lion.

name: Scottish Fold
blurb: Cat breed having specific gene mutation
fact: All Scottish Folds trace back to one barn cat named Susie - and many sit up 'Buddha style'.

name: Sphynx cat
fact: Not truly hairless - it has a fine down and feels like suede to stroke.

name: Basset Hound
fact: Its long ears drag along the ground to waft smells up toward its nose.

name: Komondor
fact: Its corded coat makes it look like a giant mop - and blend in with the flock it guards.
credit: Nikki68 at Russian Wikipedia · CC BY 2.5

name: Chinese Crested Dog
fact: Has won the World's Ugliest Dog Contest many times - it was once a sailor's ratter.

name: Xoloitzcuintle
fact: The Aztecs believed this hairless dog guided the dead through the underworld.
credit: Svenska Mässan from Sweden · CC BY 2.0

name: Puli dog
fact: Its coat naturally twists into cords - the dog underneath is surprisingly small.
credit: Original uploader was Elf at en.wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Greyhound
fact: The fastest dog breed - but famously lazy, sleeping up to 18 hours a day.

name: Budgerigar
fact: A budgie named Puck held the world record for the biggest vocabulary of any bird.

name: Sulphur-crested cockatoo
fact: A cockatoo named Snowball could dance to the beat - wild ones teach each other to open bins.

name: Moon jellyfish
fact: Has no brain, heart or bones - and its sting is too weak for most people to feel.

name: Common starfish
fact: Pushes its stomach out of its mouth to digest a mussel inside its own shell.

name: Purple sea urchin
fact: Its five-toothed jaw is called Aristotle's lantern, after his description of it.
credit: Ed Bierman from CA, usa · CC BY 2.0

name: Caribbean hermit crab
fact: Lines up with others by size to swap shells in a chain when a new one turns up.

name: American lobster
blurb: Lobster of the western North Atlantic
fact: Chews with teeth inside its stomach and tastes with its legs.
credit: OAR/National Undersea Research Program (NURP). · Public domain

name: Hummingbird hawk-moth
fact: Hovers at flowers sipping nectar so convincingly that people report seeing hummingbirds in Europe.

name: Dryocampa rubicunda
fact: Looks like it was dyed for a birthday party - adults barely eat during their short lives.

name: Common eastern firefly
fact: Males draw a J-shaped flash in the air to court females, who flash back from the grass.
credit: art farmer from evansville indiana, usa · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Giant African land snail
fact: One of the most invasive species on Earth - it eats over 500 kinds of plant.

name: Attacus atlas
fact: Adults have no mouth and live only about a week - the wing tips mimic cobra heads.

name: Psittacosaurus
fact: One of the best-known dinosaurs - a fossil even preserved its skin colour: dark back, pale belly.

name: Protoceratops
fact: Found locked in combat with a Velociraptor, both buried mid-fight by a collapsing dune.
credit: Tadek Kurpaski from London, Poland · CC BY 2.0

name: Compsognathus
fact: Chicken-sized - one fossil was found with a whole lizard still in its stomach.
credit: Zach Tirrell from Plymouth, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Nigersaurus
fact: Its wide, straight-edged mouth mowed plants at ground level like a lawnmower.

name: Quokka
fact: Its upturned mouth makes it look like it is always smiling - selfies with it are a tourist rite.

name: Common wombat
fact: Produces cube-shaped poop and stacks it on rocks to mark its territory.

name: Tasmanian devil
fact: Has one of the strongest bites of any mammal for its size - it eats bones, fur and all.

name: Sugar glider
fact: Glides between trees on a skin membrane stretched from wrist to ankle.

name: Naked mole-rat
fact: Lives in colonies with a queen like bees, almost never gets cancer, and barely ages.

name: Malayan tapir
fact: Its black-and-white body breaks up its outline in moonlit jungle.

name: Greater roadrunner
fact: Can kill and eat rattlesnakes - it grabs them by the tail and whips their heads on rocks.

name: Kea
blurb: Species of bird endemic to New Zealand
fact: The world's only alpine parrot - famous for pulling the rubber off car windscreens.

name: Scotoplanes
blurb: Genus of deep-sea sea cucumbers known as sea pigs
fact: A deep-sea cucumber that walks on puffy water-filled legs, in herds.

name: Christmas Island red crab
fact: Each year tens of millions march to the sea at once, with crab bridges built over the roads.

name: Bombardier beetle
fact: Mixes chemicals in its abdomen to blast a boiling, popping spray at attackers.

name: Glasswing butterfly
fact: Its glassy wings are almost invisible in flight - the glasswing butterfly.

name: Sword-billed hummingbird
blurb: Species of bird from South America
fact: The only bird with a bill longer than its body - it has to groom with its feet.
credit: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK · CC BY 2.0

name: Banded archerfish
fact: Knocks insects off leaves with a jet of water spat from below the surface.

name: Ocellaris clownfish
fact: All clownfish are born male - when the group's female dies, the top male becomes her.

name: White-spotted pufferfish
fact: Males spend a week sculpting 2-metre circles in the sand with their fins to court females.
credit: Hiroshi Kawase, Yuki Kitajima, Daisuke Iwai · CC BY 4.0

name: Atlantic hagfish
fact: Can turn a bucket of seawater into slime in seconds - and ties itself in knots to clean off.

name: Pygmy marmoset
fact: The smallest monkey in the world - it gnaws holes in trees to drink the sap.

name: Philippine tarsier
fact: Each eyeball is bigger than its brain - and its eyes can't move, so it turns its head.

name: Mata mata
fact: Lies still on the river bed and sucks fish into its mouth like a vacuum cleaner.

name: Common basilisk
fact: Runs across the surface of water on its hind legs before sinking.

name: Frilled lizard
fact: Flares a huge frill, hisses - and if that fails, sprints away upright on its hind legs.
credit: Matt from Melbourne, Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Wallace's flying frog
fact: Glides between trees using its giant webbed feet as parachutes.

name: Surinam toad
fact: The eggs sink into the skin of the mother's back, and fully formed toadlets pop out of it.

name: Chambered nautilus
fact: A living fossil that floats by adjusting gas in the chambers of its shell.

name: Alvinella pompejana
fact: One of the most heat-tolerant complex animals - its tail sits in near-boiling vent water.
credit: National Science Foundation (University of Delaware College of Marine Studies) · Public domain

name: Atlantic horseshoe crab
fact: Its blue blood is used to test medicines and vaccines for bacteria.

name: Aardvark
fact: First in the dictionary - and can dig a burrow faster than a team of men with spades.

name: Southern cassowary
fact: Often called the most dangerous bird - its inner toe carries a 12 cm dagger-like claw.

name: Coconut crab
fact: The largest land invertebrate - its pinch is one of the strongest of any animal.

name: Hercules beetle
fact: One of the longest beetles in the world - males wrestle with their huge pincer-like horns.

name: Bullet ant
fact: Its sting tops the Schmidt pain index - it feels like being shot.

name: Electric eel
blurb: Genus of fishes in South America
fact: Not a true eel - it's a knifefish that can leap out of the water to shock threats.

name: Wilson's bird-of-paradise
fact: Its bare blue skull looks like a bright cap - and the male clears a dance floor in the forest.

name: Snowy albatross
fact: Has the longest wingspan of any living bird and can glide for hours without flapping.

name: Andean condor
fact: One condor flew over 170 km without flapping its wings once.

name: Giant armadillo
fact: Has the largest claw of any living animal for its size.

name: Gaur
blurb: Largest species of the bovid family
fact: The largest wild cattle in the world - even tigers usually avoid adults.

name: Bighorn sheep
blurb: Species of sheep native to North America
fact: Rams smash heads at over 30 km/h - a double-layered skull absorbs the blow.

name: Reef stonefish
fact: The world's most venomous fish - it looks exactly like a lumpy rock.

name: Giant moray
fact: Has a second set of jaws in its throat that shoot forward to drag prey down.

name: Atlantic bluefin tuna
fact: Keeps its body warmer than the sea around it - and crosses the Atlantic.

name: Giant oarfish
fact: The longest bony fish in the world - likely the source of many sea serpent tales.

name: Ascarosepion pfefferi
fact: Ripples with flashing purple and yellow and walks along the seabed instead of swimming.

name: Bobbit worm
fact: Hides in the sand with only its jaws showing, then snaps up passing fish.

name: Wandering glider dragonfly
fact: A dragonfly that migrates across oceans - the longest-distance flyer of any insect.
credit: Jeevan Jose, Kerala, India · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Pronghorn
blurb: Species of North American hoofed mammal
fact: The fastest land animal in the Americas - probably evolved to outrun the extinct American cheetah.

name: White-throated needletail
fact: Possibly the fastest bird in flapping flight - it rarely lands except to nest.

name: Common pipistrelle
fact: Small enough to squeeze through a gap the width of a pencil, yet eats thousands of midges a night.

name: House sparrow
fact: Has followed humans so closely for 10,000 years that it barely lives anywhere people don't.

name: Rock dove (pigeon)
fact: Every city pigeon is descended from escaped domestic birds - wild cliff-nesting rock doves are now rare.

name: European robin
fact: Follows gardeners around to snatch worms they dig up - a habit it once had with wild boar.

name: Common starling
fact: All 200 million North American starlings descend from ~100 birds released in Central Park in 1890.

name: Mallard
fact: Ancestor of almost every domestic duck breed, including the white Pekin.
credit: This picture was realized by Richard Bartz by using a Canon EF 70-300mm f/4-5.6  · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: Slow worm
fact: Looks like a snake but blinks - it's a legless lizard, and one lived 54 years in a zoo.

name: Common shrew
fact: Shrinks its own skull and brain in winter to save energy, then regrows them in spring.

name: Eurasian harvest mouse
fact: The only Old World mammal with a gripping tail, used like a fifth hand while climbing stalks.

name: Hazel dormouse
fact: Spends up to three-quarters of its life asleep.

name: Brown rat
fact: Can tread water for three days and survive being flushed down a toilet.

name: Red squirrel
blurb: Species of tree squirrel common in Europe and Asia
fact: Forgets so many of its buried nuts that it plants whole forests.

name: European mole
fact: Keeps larders of hundreds of live worms, paralysed by a bite to the head.

name: Eurasian wren
fact: Tiny, yet its song is about ten times louder, weight for weight, than a cockerel crowing.

name: Blue jay
fact: Isn't actually blue - the colour comes from light scattering in its feathers.

name: Black-capped chickadee
blurb: Species of small, non-migratory, North American passerine
fact: Grows new brain cells every autumn to remember where it hid its food.
credit: No machine-readable author provided. Mdf assumed (based on copyright claims). · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Zebra finch
fact: One of the most-studied birds in science, because baby males learn to sing much as human babies learn to talk.

name: Gouldian finch
fact: Babies have glowing-looking spots inside their mouths that help parents feed them in dark nests.

name: Common goldfish
fact: Can be trained to respond to sounds and colours - the three-second memory is a myth.

name: Guppy
fact: Has been released to eat mosquito larvae in so many places that it now lives on every continent but Antarctica.

name: Atlantic mudskipper
fact: A fish that spends most of its time out of the water, walking on its fins across mudflats.

name: Leopard slug
fact: Mates while dangling in mid-air from a thick rope of slime, the pair entwined.

name: European garden spider
fact: Eats its own web every evening to recycle the silk proteins, then spins a new one.

name: Zebra jumping spider
fact: Hunts by sight, stalking flies like a tiny cat before pouncing - with a silk safety line attached.

name: Buff-tailed bumblebee
fact: Can 'buzz pollinate' - vibrating flowers so hard pollen shakes loose, which tomatoes need.

name: Sacred scarab
fact: Steers its dung ball in a straight line using the Milky Way.

name: European stag beetle
fact: Spends up to six years as a grub in dead wood, then lives only a few weeks as an adult.

name: American cockroach
fact: One of the fastest running insects - about 50 body lengths a second.

name: Madagascar hissing cockroach
fact: Hisses by pushing air out through the breathing holes on its sides.
credit: Almabes at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Desert locust
fact: Switches from shy loner to swarming plague when crowded - even changing colour.

name: Painted lady
fact: Flies from tropical Africa to the Arctic Circle and back over several generations.

name: Luna moth
fact: Has no mouth as an adult - it lives about a week just to find a mate.

name: African death's-head hawkmoth
fact: Raids beehives for honey and squeaks like a mouse - it's the moth on The Silence of the Lambs poster.

name: Domestic silk moth
blurb: Moth mainly used in the production of silk
fact: So thoroughly domesticated that the adult moths can no longer fly or survive in the wild.

name: Giant African millipede
fact: One of the largest millipedes - it curls into a spiral and oozes irritants when bothered.

name: House centipede
fact: Lassos prey with its long legs - a free pest-control service hiding in your bathroom.

name: Serama
fact: The smallest chicken breed - it struts with its chest pushed out like a tiny soldier.

name: Golden hamster
fact: Nearly every pet hamster descends from one litter dug up in Syria in 1930.
credit: Adamjennison111 at English Wikipedia · CC BY 2.5

name: Long-tailed chinchilla
fact: Has the densest fur of any land animal - so thick fleas can't live in it.

name: Munchkin cat
fact: Its short legs come from a natural mutation found in a stray cat in Louisiana.

name: Chihuahua
fact: The smallest dog breed, and one of the longest-lived.
credit: Bonnie van den Born, http://www.bonfoto.nl. The original uploader was Cwazi at D · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: French Bulldog
fact: Most can't swim, because their heavy front ends tip them nose-down.

name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
fact: The only dog breed named after a fictional character.

name: Falabella
fact: A true horse, not a pony, despite being smaller than many dogs.

name: Rock hyrax
blurb: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East
fact: A guinea-pig-sized animal whose closest living relatives are elephants.

name: Lesser Egyptian jerboa
fact: Bounds across the Sahara on kangaroo-like back legs and gets nearly all its water from food.

name: American pika
fact: Doesn't hibernate - it spends summer drying hay piles to eat under the snow.

name: Kitti's hog-nosed bat
fact: Possibly the smallest mammal on Earth, about the size of a bumblebee.
credit: Jan Ebr & Ivana Ebrová · CC BY 4.0

name: Hammer-headed bat
blurb: Megabat widely distributed in West and Central Africa
fact: Males have huge boxy heads that work as amplifiers for their honking mating calls.
credit: Sarah H. Olson, Gerard Bounga, Alain Ondzie, Trent Bushmaker, Stephanie N. Seife · CC0

name: Tokay gecko
fact: Named after its loud bark-like 'to-kay' call.

name: Pig-nosed turtle
fact: A freshwater turtle with a pig snout and flippers like a sea turtle.

name: Tomato frog
fact: Puffs up and oozes a glue that gums up the mouth of anything that bites it.
credit: Franco Andreone - [:it:Wikipedia:Autorizzazioni_ottenute/Franco_Andreone see aut · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: African clawed frog
fact: Was used as a pregnancy test in the 1930s-50s - it laid eggs when injected with a pregnant woman's urine.

name: Desert rain frog
fact: Squeaks like a dog toy when threatened.

name: Fire salamander
fact: Named because it crawled out of burning logs, leading people to believe it was born from fire.

name: Pacific spiny lumpsucker
fact: A tiny round fish that clings to rocks with a suction cup made from its fins.

name: Sheepshead
fact: Has eerily human-looking teeth, used to crush shellfish.

name: Four-eyed fish
fact: Swims at the surface with each eye half in the air and half in the water.

stats.label: Sees
stats.value: Above and below water at once

name: Big-belly seahorse
fact: The father gets pregnant and gives birth to hundreds of babies.
credit: Mark Norman / Museum Victoria · CC BY 3.0

name: Longhorn cowfish
fact: Encased in a rigid bony box, it swims by sculling with its small fins.

name: Spotted garden eel
fact: Colonies sway like a field of grass and all vanish into their burrows when a diver approaches.

name: Common fangtooth
fact: Its fangs are so long it has sockets in its skull so it can close its mouth.

stats.label: Teeth
stats.value: Largest for body size of any fish

name: Sea lamprey
blurb: Species of fish native to the Northern Hemisphere
fact: A jawless sucker-mouthed fish older than dinosaurs.

name: Spanish dancer
fact: Swims by rippling its red body like a flamenco dancer's skirt.

name: Christmas tree worm
fact: Its two feathery spirals vanish into its coral tube in an instant if anything comes near.

name: Thorn bug
fact: Looks exactly like a rose thorn, so birds pass it by.
credit: Marshal Hedin from San Diego · CC BY 2.0

name: 17-year periodical cicada
fact: Spends 17 years underground, then billions emerge in the same few weeks.

name: Puss caterpillar
fact: Looks like a fluffy wig but hides venomous spines under the fur.

name: Diving bell spider
fact: The only spider that lives entirely underwater, in a silk bubble of air it builds.

name: Ogre-faced spider
fact: Holds a silk net in its front legs and throws it over passing prey.

stats.label: Hunts with
stats.value: A net held in its legs

name: Marabou stork
fact: One of the largest wingspans of any land bird - and often called the ugliest.

name: Eurasian hoopoe
fact: Nestlings defend themselves by squirting foul-smelling liquid at intruders.
credit: Greg Schechter from San Francisco, USA · CC BY 2.0

name: Tawny frogmouth
fact: Often mistaken for an owl, it poses as a broken branch with its eyes shut to slits.

name: Burrowing owl
fact: Hisses like a rattlesnake from inside its burrow to scare off predators.

name: Elf owl
fact: The lightest owl in the world, nesting in old woodpecker holes in saguaro cacti.

name: Common swift
fact: Can stay in the air for ten months straight, eating, drinking and sleeping on the wing.

name: Monk parakeet
fact: The only parrot that builds stick nests - whole colonies share one giant apartment block.

name: Chinese water deer
fact: Instead of antlers, males grow long fang-like tusks.

name: Lesser mouse-deer
fact: The smallest hoofed mammal - about the size of a rabbit.

name: Gerenuk
fact: Stands upright on its back legs to browse leaves out of reach of other antelope.

name: Red river hog
fact: Bright orange with long white ear tufts - the punk of the pig world.

name: Kinkajou
fact: Uses its long tongue to lap nectar - and its gripping tail to hang from branches.
credit: Dick Culbert from Gibsons, B.C., Canada · CC BY 2.0

name: Cookiecutter shark
fact: Takes perfectly round bites out of whales, tuna - and even submarines.

name: Epaulette shark
fact: Walks across reef flats on its fins at low tide, surviving hours with little oxygen.

name: Green iguana
fact: Has a light-sensing third eye on top of its head.

name: Armadillo girdled lizard
fact: Rolls into a ball by biting its own tail, like a tiny armadillo.

name: Flying dragon lizard
fact: Glides between trees on wings made of skin stretched over its extended ribs.

name: Common blue-tongued skink
fact: Sticks out its bright blue tongue to scare predators.

name: Takin
fact: Inspired by legend to have been made from a goat's head and a cow's body.

name: Common warthog
blurb: Wild member of the pig family
fact: Backs into burrows bottom-first so it can charge out tusks-first.

name: Gila monster
blurb: Largest species of lizard in the United States
fact: A hormone in its saliva led to the diabetes drug exenatide and its successors.

stats.label: Big meals
stats.value: A third of its yearly food at once

name: Tuatara
fact: Looks like a lizard but is the last survivor of a group that thrived with the dinosaurs.
credit: Sid Mosdell from New Zealand · CC BY 2.0

name: Goliath beetle
fact: One of the heaviest insects - its larvae weigh as much as a hamster.

name: Titan beetle
fact: Its jaws can snap a pencil in half - and nobody has found its larvae.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Brazilian wandering spider
fact: Wanders the forest floor at night instead of building a web - and sometimes ends up in banana shipments.

name: Tarantula hawk
blurb: Common name for two genera of wasps
fact: Paralyses tarantulas to feed its young - its sting is rated 'blinding, fierce, shockingly electric'.

name: Emerald cockroach wasp
fact: Stings a cockroach's brain, then walks it like a dog on a leash to its burrow.

name: Giant isopod
fact: A giant deep-sea woodlouse - one in a Japanese aquarium went five years without eating.
credit: NOAA Office of Ocean Exploration and Research · Public domain

name: Queen Alexandra's birdwing
fact: The largest butterfly in the world - the first was shot down with a shotgun.

name: Greater flamingo
fact: Eats with its head upside down, filtering food through its bill.

name: Arctic tern
blurb: Bird that breeds in the Arctic and subarctic and migrates to the Antarctic
fact: Has the longest migration of any animal - pole to pole and back each year.

name: Magnificent frigatebird
fact: Males inflate a huge red throat balloon to attract females.
credit: Andrew Turner from Washington, DC, United States · CC BY 2.0

name: Emu
blurb: Large flightless bird endemic to Australia
fact: Australia's army fought emus in 1932 with machine guns - and lost.

name: Arapaima
fact: Its armoured scales are so tough that piranha bites can't pierce them.

name: Wels catfish
fact: Some in France lunge out of the river to catch pigeons on the bank.
credit: Dieter Florian (To contact the author, ask the uploader or take a look at tauchs · CC BY-SA 3.0 de

name: Humpback anglerfish
fact: The female dangles a glowing lure in the pitch black - the deep-sea anglerfish of Finding Nemo.

name: Eastern brown snake
blurb: Highly venomous snake native to Australia
fact: Causes more deaths than any other snake in Australia.

name: Beluga sturgeon
blurb: Species of fish in the sturgeon family
fact: One of the largest freshwater fish ever - and the source of the world's most expensive caviar.
credit: あおもりくま（Aomorikuma） · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Fox squirrel
fact: Its bones glow pink under ultraviolet light, from a harmless pigment build-up.

name: Northern cardinal
fact: Will spend hours attacking its own reflection in a window, sure it is a rival.

name: American robin
fact: Finds worms mostly by sight, tilting its head to watch the soil for movement.

name: Barn swallow
fact: Drinks and even bathes by skimming the surface of a pond in mid-flight.

name: Eurasian blue tit
fact: In 20th-century Britain, blue tits learned to peck open milk bottle tops - and the trick spread across the country.

name: Eurasian magpie
fact: One of the few non-mammals known to recognise itself in a mirror.

name: Wood duck
fact: A day after hatching, its ducklings leap from their tree hole - sometimes over 15 m - and bounce unharmed.

stats.label: Nests
stats.value: In tree holes up to ~20 m up

credit: Chuck Homler d/b/a FocusOnwWildlife · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Mandarin duck
fact: Pairs were given as wedding gifts in China as a symbol of a loyal marriage.

name: Common kingfisher
fact: Its beak's shape inspired the nose of Japan's 500 Series bullet train, which made it quieter.

name: Northern mockingbird
fact: Can learn hundreds of songs, including car alarms and squeaky gates.

name: American goldfinch
fact: One of the few birds that changes its whole plumage twice a year - bright yellow in summer, olive in winter. It's also the state bird of Iowa.

name: Indian peafowl
fact: The peacock rattles its whole train to make a low rumble females can feel.
credit: Kandukuru Nagarjun from Bangalore, India · CC BY 2.0

name: European rabbit
fact: The wild ancestor of every pet rabbit - and it eats its own soft droppings to get a second go at its food.

name: European hare
blurb: Large species of hare native to Europe and parts of Asia
fact: The famous 'mad March hares' boxing in spring are usually females fending off pushy males.

name: Snowshoe hare
fact: Its giant furry hind feet work like snowshoes, so it can run on top of deep snow.

stats.label: Coat
stats.value: Brown in summer, white in winter

credit: Lepus_americanus_5459.JPG: Walter Siegmund (talk) derivative work: Wsiegmund · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Groundhog
fact: In hibernation its heart drops from ~80 beats a minute to about 5 - and 'Groundhog Day' asks it to forecast spring.

name: Red-backed salamander
fact: Has no lungs at all - it breathes through its skin - and in some eastern US forests the salamanders' total weight beats that of the birds.

stats.label: Numbers
stats.value: Outweigh all birds in some forests

name: Spotted salamander
fact: Green algae grow inside its eggs - and even inside the embryos - feeding them oxygen.
credit: D. Gordon E. Robertson · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Eastern newt
fact: Spends a few years on land as a bright orange 'red eft' before returning to water as an adult.

name: Wood frog
fact: Freezes solid in winter - heart stopped, no breathing - then thaws and hops off in spring.

name: Common garter snake
fact: In Manitoba, tens of thousands emerge from dens together in spring - the largest snake gathering on Earth.

name: Painted turtle
fact: Hatchlings can spend their first winter in the nest, partly frozen, and survive.

name: Diamondback terrapin
fact: The only US turtle that lives in salty tidal marshes - it has a gland to cry out the extra salt.

name: Common eastern bumblebee
fact: 'Buzz pollinates' tomatoes by vibrating its flight muscles until the pollen shakes out.
credit: USGS Bee Inventory and Monitoring Lab from Beltsville, Maryland, USA · Public domain

name: Mourning cloak
fact: One of the longest-lived butterflies - it freezes into a sort of hibernation and flies on warm winter days.
credit: Pavel Kirillov from St.Petersburg, Russia · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Long-tailed tit
blurb: Species of bird in Europe and Asia
fact: Builds a stretchy dome nest of moss and spider silk, lined with up to ~2,000 feathers - and on cold nights a flock huddles in a row on one branch.

name: Red admiral
fact: Gets tipsy on fermenting fruit and becomes so slow you can pick it up.

name: Green darner
fact: Migrates down North America in huge swarms - and the trip takes 3 generations.

name: Silverfish
blurb: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma
fact: Can live a year without food, nibbling the glue out of book bindings when it does eat.

name: Isabella tiger moth
fact: Its caterpillar, the 'woolly bear', freezes solid in winter and thaws in spring - and folklore says its stripes predict the winter.
credit: Andy Reago & Chrissy McClarren · CC BY 2.0

name: Koi
fact: A single prize koi sold for about $1.8 million in 2018.

name: Common carp
fact: Has no teeth in its mouth - it chews with teeth in its throat.

name: Rainbow trout
fact: Some rainbow trout go to sea and come back huge, as 'steelhead'.
credit: Engbretson Eric, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service · Public domain

name: Atlantic salmon
fact: Finds its way back to the very stream it hatched in - by smell - to spawn.

name: Northern pike
fact: An ambush hunter with hundreds of backward-pointing teeth - it eats ducklings from below.

stats.label: Ambush speed
stats.value: Strikes in a fraction of a second

name: Channel catfish
fact: Covered in taste buds - it's basically a swimming tongue.

name: Neon tetra
fact: Its glowing stripe dims at night when it rests, and brightens when it wakes.

name: Suckermouth catfish
fact: Clings to rocks - and aquarium glass - with a suction-cup mouth while it scrapes off algae.
credit: Raphaël Covain, Natural History Museum of Geneva · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Holstein Friesian
fact: The black-and-white dairy cow - no two have the same pattern of patches.

name: Dalmatian
fact: Born completely white - the spots appear over the first few weeks.

name: Poodle
fact: Its fancy haircut began as practical swim gear - fur left only to keep joints and organs warm in cold water.
credit: Tim Wilson from Blaine, MN, USA · CC BY 2.0

name: Labrador Retriever
blurb: British breed of retriever gun dog
fact: Uses its thick tail like a rudder when it swims.
credit: IDS.photos from Tiverton, UK · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Golden Retriever
fact: Bred for such a 'soft mouth' that it can carry a raw egg without cracking it.

stats.label: Mouth
stats.value: So soft it carries eggs unbroken

credit: Dukedestiny01.jpg: "Janneke Vreugdenhil" derivative work: Anka Friedrich ([[User · Public domain

name: Beagle
fact: Its nose is so good that airports use it to sniff out food in luggage.

name: Siberian Husky
fact: Huskies helped carry diphtheria medicine 1,000 km to Nome, Alaska, in 1925.

stats.label: Eyes
stats.value: Often blue, or one of each

name: Persian cat
fact: Its flat face makes it pick up food with the underside of its tongue.
credit: The original uploader was Lajoma at Finnish Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Bengal cat
fact: Many Bengals have a 'glitter' coat that sparkles in the sun - and they often like water.

name: Clydesdale horse
fact: Its 'feathered' feet are the size of dinner plates.

name: Nigerian Dwarf goat
fact: A tiny goat whose milk is so creamy it is prized for cheese and soap.

name: Ayam Cemani
fact: Black feathers, skin, beak, tongue, organs and bones - due to a gene that floods its tissues with pigment.

name: Common chuckwalla
blurb: Large lizard native to the Sonoran and Mojave Deserts
fact: Wedges itself into a rock crack and inflates its lungs, so nothing can pull it out.

name: Superb fairywren
fact: Mothers sing a password to their eggs, and chicks must call it back to be fed - cuckoo chicks can't.

name: Northern gannet
fact: Plunge-dives into the sea at about 100 km/h, cushioned by air sacs under its skin.

name: Bohemian waxwing
blurb: Passerine bird from Eurasia and North America
fact: Eats so many fermented berries that it sometimes gets drunk - its liver is unusually large to cope.
credit: Tatiana Bulyonkova from Novosibirsk, Russia · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Nicobar pigeon
fact: The dodo's closest living relative.

name: Green sea turtle
fact: Named for the green colour of its fat, from a diet of seagrass.

name: Moorish idol
fact: The model for Gill in Finding Nemo.

name: Hellbender
fact: Breathes through its baggy, wrinkled skin - hence nicknames like 'snot otter'.

name: Menelaus blue morpho
fact: Its electric blue has no pigment at all - just nanostructures bending light.

name: Leafcutter ant
fact: Doesn't eat the leaves it carries - it farms a fungus on them.

name: Weaver ant
fact: Workers hold larvae like glue guns, using their silk to stitch leaves into nests.

name: Sunflower sea star
fact: One of the fastest sea stars - and it has up to 24 arms.
credit: Jerry Kirkhart from Los Osos, Calif. · CC BY 2.0

name: Greater bilby
fact: Its pouch faces backwards so it does not fill with soil when it digs.

name: Humphead wrasse
fact: One of few fish that eats crown-of-thorns starfish and boxfish, toxins and all.
credit: Julien Bidet for MDC Seamarc · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Sea angel
fact: A see-through 'sea angel' snail that flaps wing-like fins - and grabs prey with tentacles from its head.

stats.label: Hunt
stats.value: Six tentacles shoot from its head

credit: Kevin Raskoff, Hidden Ocean 2005 Expedition: NOAA Office of Ocean Exploration. · Public domain

name: Eastern hognose snake
fact: If you flip it right side up while it's 'dead', it rolls straight back over.

name: Eastern gray squirrel
blurb: Species of squirrel native to North America
fact: Fakes burying nuts when it thinks it's being watched, to fool would-be thieves.

name: Common bottlenose dolphin
fact: Each dolphin has a signature whistle that works as its name.

name: Fossa
blurb: Cat-like species of mammal from Madagascar
fact: Looks like a cat but is closer to mongooses; its ankles rotate so it can run down trees head first.

name: Sunda pangolin
blurb: Species of pangolin found in southeast Asia
fact: Rolls into an armoured ball that even lions struggle to open.

name: Capybara
fact: The world's largest rodent, famously calm - other animals often sit on it.

name: Southern sea otter
fact: Floats on its back holding hands with other otters so nobody drifts off while asleep.
credit: Marshal Hedin from San Diego · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Kākāpō
fact: A flightless, nocturnal parrot that smells of honey - every single one has a name.

name: Northern glass frog
fact: While it sleeps it hides almost all its red blood cells in its liver, turning nearly invisible.

name: Spix's macaw
blurb: Species of macaw that is extinct in the wild
fact: Declared extinct in the wild in 2019, then released back into Brazil in 2022.
credit: Rüdiger Stehn from Kiel, Deutschland · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Okapi
fact: Looks like a zebra but is the giraffe's only living relative - and licks its own ears clean.

name: Aye-aye
fact: Taps on bark and listens for hollow grub tunnels, like an echo-locating woodpecker.

name: Chinese giant salamander
fact: The largest amphibian in the world - and it can bark like a baby.

name: Star-nosed mole
fact: The fastest eater known - it can find and eat a morsel in under a quarter of a second.

name: Hoatzin
blurb: Species of bird in South America
fact: Ferments leaves in its gut like a cow, giving it a smell like manure.

name: Leatherback sea turtle
fact: The largest turtle alive, with a rubbery shell instead of a hard one, and it lives mostly on jellyfish.
credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Southeast Region · Public domain

name: Sumatran rhinoceros
fact: The hairy rhino - the closest living relative of the extinct woolly rhinoceros.

name: Blue whale
blurb: Species of whale; largest animal known
fact: The largest animal that has ever lived - bigger than any dinosaur.

name: Water bear (tardigrade)
fact: A 'water bear' that survived a trip to open space in 2007.
credit: Schokraie E, Warnken U, Hotz-Wagenblatt A, Grohme MA, Hengherr S, et al. (2012) · CC BY 2.5

name: Mimic octopus
fact: Impersonates lionfish, sea snakes and flatfish, picking whichever scares off the current threat.

name: Blue dragon sea slug
fact: The 'blue dragon' eats Portuguese man o' war and stores their stinging cells to use itself.
credit: Taro Taylor from Sydney, Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Platypus
fact: A venomous, egg-laying mammal with a duck bill - and it glows blue-green under UV light.

name: Indo-Pacific sailfish
fact: Hunts in packs, raising its sail to herd sardines and slashing through them with its bill.

name: Hyacinth macaw
fact: The largest flying parrot in the world.

name: Japanese spider crab
fact: Has the longest legs of any arthropod.

name: Highland cattle
fact: Its long fringe (a 'dossan') keeps flies and rain out of its eyes.

name: Corn snake
fact: Named after the pattern on its belly, which looks like kernels of Indian corn.

name: Striped skunk
fact: Stamps its feet and fakes charges first - it would rather not waste its spray.

name: Maine Coon
fact: One of the biggest domestic cats - one held the record for longest cat at 123 cm.

name: Shiba Inu
fact: The dog behind the 'Doge' meme - it lets out a dramatic scream when it doesn't get its way.
credit: Takashiba at English Wikipedia · Public domain

name: Border Collie
fact: A Border Collie named Chaser learned the names of over a thousand toys.

name: Cockatiel
fact: Learns whistled tunes more readily than words - its crest flattens or rises with its mood.
credit: Photo by: Ganatron – paulweberphoto.com · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: European praying mantis
fact: Has a single ear in the middle of its chest, tuned to hear hunting bats.

name: Common raccoon dog
fact: The only dog-family animal that hibernates - and it can climb trees.

name: Common raven
blurb: Large, black species of passerine bird
fact: Plays games like sliding down snowy roofs on its back - just for fun.

name: Ring-tailed lemur
fact: Males rub their tails with scent from their wrists and wave them at rivals in stink fights.

name: Sunda slow loris
blurb: Species of primate found in South East Asia
fact: One of the only venomous primates - it licks a gland in its elbow to make a toxic bite.
credit: David Haring / Duke Lemur Center · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Brown-throated sloth
fact: Climbs down once a week to poop, and its fur is home to algae and moths.

name: Meerkat
blurb: Species of mongoose from Southern Africa
fact: Teaches its young to eat scorpions by bringing them dead ones, then disarmed ones, then live ones.

name: Proboscis monkey
fact: The male's huge drooping nose amplifies its honking calls - and impresses females.

name: Japanese macaque
fact: The world's most northerly non-human primate - some troops bathe in hot springs in winter.

name: Mandrill
blurb: Species of Old World monkey from Africa
fact: The largest monkey - mandrills gather in the biggest primate groups ever recorded.

name: Gelada
fact: The only primate that lives mostly on grass - herds of hundreds graze on cliff tops.

name: Golden snub-nosed monkey
fact: Its flat, upturned nose may help it avoid frostbite in the snowy mountains of China.

name: Binturong
blurb: Asian mammal also known as a bearcat
fact: Smells exactly like buttered popcorn - from the same chemical in its urine.

name: Kirk's dik-dik
fact: Named after its whistling alarm call - and mates for life.

name: Ocean sunfish
fact: The heaviest bony fish - it looks like a giant swimming head with fins.
credit: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration · Public domain

name: Orchid mantis
fact: Looks so much like an orchid that insects fly straight to it - more than to real flowers.

name: Walrus
blurb: Species of marine mammal with tusks
fact: Uses its tusks to haul itself out of the water onto the ice.

name: West Indian manatee
fact: Its closest living relatives are elephants - and sailors once mistook it for mermaids.

name: Dugong
fact: The only strictly plant-eating marine mammal - it grazes seagrass meadows like a sea cow.

name: Beluga whale
fact: Chirps, whistles and clicks so much sailors called it the sea canary.
credit: Javier Yaya Tur / CIUDAD DE LAS ARTES Y LAS CIENCIAS from Valencia, España · CC BY 2.0

name: Emperor tamarin
fact: Named as a joke for its likeness to the moustached German emperor.

name: Honduran white bat
blurb: Species of bat that constructs tents
fact: Snips leaves so they fold into tents, where little huddles of white bats sleep.

name: Texas horned lizard
fact: Squirts blood from its eyes at coyotes and dogs - the blood tastes foul to them.
credit: Patrick Alexander from Las Cruces, NM · CC0

name: Argentine horned frog
fact: Its mouth is so big it tries to eat things nearly its own size - sometimes fatally.
credit: Melanie Mae Bryan from Greensboro, NC, USA · CC BY 2.0

name: Muskox
fact: Herds form a circle with horns facing out and the calves in the middle.

name: Red lionfish
fact: Invaded the Atlantic and Caribbean - people are now encouraged to catch and eat it.
credit: Photo by Jens Petersen, Edited by User:Olegiwit (cloned in part of fins) and Fir · CC BY 2.5

name: Margay
fact: Can turn its ankles round to run head-first down a tree trunk like a squirrel.

name: Iguanodon
fact: Its thumb spike was first put on its nose - one of the earliest dinosaurs ever named.

name: Yutyrannus
fact: A giant tyrannosaur relative covered in fluffy feathers - the largest feathered animal known.
credit: Laika ac from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Borealopelta
fact: So well preserved it's called a dinosaur mummy - even its last meal of ferns survived.

stats.label: Preserved
stats.value: Like a statue - skin and armour

credit: Nobu Tamura email:nobu.tamura@yahoo.com http://spinops.blogspot.com/ · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Markhor
fact: Its name may mean "snake-eater" - its corkscrew horns are some of the most spectacular of any goat.

name: Northern giant hornet
blurb: Predatory hornet, largest in the world
fact: A small group can wipe out an entire honey-bee hive in a few hours.

name: Frilled shark
fact: A living fossil with the longest known pregnancy of any vertebrate.
credit: This illustration was made by Citron You must credit this : Citron / CC-BY-SA-3. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Alligator snapping turtle
fact: Lies still with its mouth open, wiggling a pink worm-like lure on its tongue to catch fish.
credit: Gary M. Stolz/U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service · Public domain

name: Bearded vulture
fact: Eats bones - and drops big ones from great heights onto rocks to crack them open.

name: Blakiston's fish owl
fact: The world's largest owl species - it wades in icy rivers to catch fish.

name: Common vampire bat
blurb: Species of bat native to the Americas
fact: Shares blood meals with roostmates who went hungry - and remembers who helped it.

name: Dhole
fact: A whistling wild dog whose packs can drive off tigers.

name: Giant anteater
fact: Flicks its tongue 150 times a minute and eats up to 30,000 ants and termites a day.

name: African buffalo
fact: Herds vote on where to go next by standing up and facing their chosen direction.

name: Southern elephant seal
fact: The largest seal - males roar through an inflatable trunk-like nose.

name: Moose
fact: Can dive nearly 6 metres to eat water plants - and swims for kilometres.

name: Deinonychus
fact: Its discovery convinced scientists dinosaurs were fast and active, and related to birds.

name: Deinocheirus
fact: Known only from giant arms for 50 years - the rest turned out to have a hump and a duck bill.

name: Inland taipan
blurb: Extremely venomous snake native to Australia
fact: Has the most toxic venom of any snake - but is so shy that bites are almost unknown.

name: Hippopotamus
fact: Among Africa's most dangerous animals - and it secretes a red, sunscreen-like 'blood sweat'.

name: Swordfish
blurb: Fish which has a long, pointed bill
fact: Has special organs that heat its eyes and brain for hunting in cold, deep water.

name: Steller's sea eagle
blurb: Bird of prey species native to East Asia
fact: One of the heaviest eagles in the world, with a giant golden-orange beak.

name: Gyrfalcon
fact: The largest falcon - in medieval falconry, only kings could fly one.
credit: Falco_rusticolus_white.jpg: Ólafur Larsen derivative work: Bogbumper (talk) · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Leopard seal
fact: The only seal that regularly hunts other warm-blooded animals - it has a reptile-like grin.

name: Golden eagle
fact: Has been known to take down deer - one of the most widespread and powerful eagles.

name: Black marlin
fact: One of the fastest fish in the ocean - its pectoral fins are rigid and can't be folded.
credit: Queensland State Archives from Runcorn, Queensland, Australia · Public domain

name: Australian box jellyfish
fact: One of the most venomous animals on Earth - and it has 24 eyes.
credit: Avispa marina.jpg: Guido Gautsch, Toyota, Japan derivative work: Mithril (talk) · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Common toad
fact: Walks back to the exact pond it was born in to breed - volunteers help them cross roads.

name: Ferret
fact: When excited it does a hopping, sideways 'war dance' that often ends with it crashing into furniture.

name: Ball python
fact: Curls into a tight ball with its head in the middle when scared.

name: Warty frogfish
fact: Swallows prey in about 6 milliseconds - one of the fastest strikes in nature.

stats.label: Lure
stats.value: A fishing rod on its head

name: New Zealand glowworm
fact: Lights up New Zealand caves like a starry sky - the glow lures insects into its sticky threads.

name: Great potoo
fact: Freezes upright on a branch by day, looking exactly like a dead stump.

name: Bald uakari
fact: Its bright red face shows it's healthy and free of malaria.

name: Least weasel
fact: The smallest carnivore in the world - it can kill prey 10 times its weight.

name: Stoat
fact: Dances wildly to mesmerise rabbits before it strikes.
credit: Marton Berntsen, crop by User:MPF · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Aardwolf
fact: A hyena that eats termites - up to a quarter of a million in one night.

name: Fishing cat
fact: A cat that loves water - it dives in head first to catch fish.

name: Rusty-spotted cat
blurb: Small wild cat species native to South Asia
fact: One of the smallest wild cats in the world, about half the size of a house cat.

name: Hooded seal
fact: Males inflate a red balloon out of one nostril to impress females.

name: Reindeer
fact: Its eyes change from gold in summer to blue in winter to see in the long Arctic dark.

name: Greater kudu
fact: Its corkscrew horns take about six years to grow their full two and a half turns.
credit: L0k1m0nk33 at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Springbok
blurb: Antelope of southwest and south Africa
fact: Bounces stiff-legged into the air ('pronking') to show predators it's too fit to chase.

name: Plains zebra
fact: Its stripes seem to confuse biting flies, which struggle to land on them.

name: Przewalski's horse
fact: Went extinct in the wild in the 1960s and was brought back from just a dozen zoo horses.

name: Bactrian camel
fact: Can drink 100 litres of water in about ten minutes.
credit: Christian Ursilva from Copenhagen, Denmark · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: European bison
fact: Was hunted to extinction in the wild by 1927 and brought back from zoo animals.

name: North Sulawesi babirusa
fact: Its upper tusks grow up through the top of its snout and curve back towards its face.
credit: Masteraah at German Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 2.0 de

name: Mantled howler
fact: One of the loudest land animals, though it spends most of the day resting.

name: Ocelot
fact: Salvador Dalí took his pet ocelot, Babou, to restaurants.

name: Sand cat
fact: Has fur on the soles of its feet to walk on scorching sand.

name: Sloth bear
fact: Blows away dirt and hoovers termites through a gap in its front teeth.

name: American badger
fact: Hunts as a team with coyotes - one digs, one chases.

stats.label: Digs
stats.value: Faster than a person can shovel

name: Striped hyena
fact: Raises its mane to look almost twice its size when threatened.

name: Spinner dolphin
fact: Leaps out of the water and spins up to seven times in one jump.

name: Basking shark
fact: The second-largest fish, cruising with its mouth open to filter plankton.
credit: Greg Skomal / NOAA Fisheries Service · Public domain

name: Megamouth shark
fact: Unknown until 1976, when one got tangled in a US Navy ship's anchor.

name: Sand tiger shark
fact: Embryos eat their siblings in the womb - only the strongest are born.

name: Largetooth sawfish
fact: Its saw detects the electric fields of prey and slashes through schools of fish.

name: Eastern diamondback rattlesnake
blurb: Species of reptile endemic to the southeastern US
fact: The heaviest venomous snake in the Americas.

name: Boomslang
fact: A bite killed the famous herpetologist Karl Schmidt, who kept notes as he died.

name: Mozambique spitting cobra
fact: Sprays venom accurately into an attacker's eyes from metres away.

name: Marine iguana
blurb: Species of marine reptile endemic to Galapagos Islands
fact: The only lizard that swims at sea - it sneezes out the salt it swallows.
credit: RAF-YYC from Calgary, Canada · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Sydney funnel-web spider
fact: Its venom is harmless to cats and dogs but deadly to humans.

name: Deathstalker
fact: A toxin from its venom helps surgeons light up brain tumours.
credit: This file is a work by Ester Inbar (user:ST or he:user:ST). More of my work can  · Attribution

name: Common octopus
fact: Most of its neurons are in its arms, which can taste what they touch.

name: Darwin's bark spider
fact: Spins the biggest webs known, across rivers, from the toughest biological material.

name: Laughing kookaburra
blurb: Species of kingfisher bird in Australia
fact: Kills snakes by bashing them against branches.
credit: Photo by: Paulweberphoto - paulweberphoto.com · CC BY 4.0

name: Bar-tailed godwit
fact: Holds the record for the longest nonstop bird flight - 11 days without landing.

name: Red-crowned crane
blurb: Species of large bird from East Asia
fact: Pairs leap and bow in elaborate courtship dances in the snow.
credit: Alastair Rae from London, United Kingdom · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Grey parrot
fact: Alex the parrot learned over 100 words and could count and name colours.

name: Scarlet macaw
fact: Flocks gather at riverbanks to eat clay that neutralises toxins in their food.

name: Osprey
fact: Turns caught fish head-first to make them more aerodynamic.
credit: Chuck Homler / Focus On Wildlife · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Common ostrich
fact: The fastest bird on land - its eyes are bigger than its brain.

name: Giant trevally
fact: Leaps out of the water to catch young seabirds in flight.
credit: Dr. Dwayne Meadows, NOAA/NMFS/OPR · Public domain

name: Mugger crocodile
fact: Balances sticks on its snout in nesting season to lure birds looking for twigs.

name: Galápagos tortoise
fact: Shells differ island to island - a clue that helped inspire Darwin's theory of evolution.
credit: Mfield, Matthew Field, http://www.photography.mattfield.com · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: False killer whale
blurb: Species of oceanic dolphin in the genus Pseudorca
fact: Has been seen offering fish to human divers.

name: Ethiopian wolf
fact: The world's rarest canid, hunting rodents on the roof of Africa.

name: Giant otter
fact: Family groups of these "river wolves" can drive off jaguars and kill caimans.

name: Fin whale
fact: The second-largest animal ever, and one of the fastest whales.
credit: Aqqa Rosing-Asvid - Visit Greenland · CC BY 2.0

name: Cuvier's beaked whale
fact: Holds the record for the deepest and longest dives of any mammal.

name: Giant oceanic manta ray
fact: Has the biggest brain of any fish and may recognise itself in a mirror.
credit: jon hanson from london, UK · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Black caiman
fact: The largest predator in the Amazon basin.

name: Humboldt squid
fact: Flashes red and white while hunting in huge packs - fishermen call it 'red devil'.
credit: Image courtesy of NOAA/MBARI 2006 · Public domain

name: Goliath birdeater
blurb: Species of tarantula from South America
fact: The biggest spider by mass - it hisses by rubbing the hairs on its legs.

name: Martial eagle
fact: Africa's largest eagle, able to knock a small antelope off its feet.

name: Wedge-tailed eagle
fact: Australia's largest bird of prey - it attacks mining drones.
credit: Ron Knight from Seaford, East Sussex, United Kingdom · CC BY 2.0

name: Goliath tigerfish
fact: Has huge dagger teeth and has been seen catching birds.

name: Red fox
fact: Pounces on mice under snow, and seems to aim using the Earth's magnetic field - jumps facing north-east land far more often.

stats.label: Range
stats.value: Every continent but Antarctica & S. America

name: White-tailed deer
fact: Raises its white tail like a flag when it bolts, so the rest of the herd knows to run.
credit: USDA photo by Scott Bauer · Public domain

name: Mute swan
fact: Unmarked mute swans on open water in England belong to the monarch, and are counted each July.

name: Siamese cat
fact: Its dark points are where the body is coolest - a temperature-sensitive pigment gene.

name: Alpine ibex
fact: Climbs the near-vertical walls of Italian dams to lick the salt off the stones.

name: Red deer
fact: Grows its antlers from scratch every year - one of the fastest-growing tissues known.

name: Elk
fact: Its 'bugle' is a surprisingly squeaky, whistling scream for such a huge animal.

name: Wild boar
fact: Its upper and lower tusks grind against each other, keeping them razor sharp.

name: White-nosed coati
fact: Can turn its ankles backwards to climb down trees head-first.
credit: Chuck Homler, Focus On Wildlife · CC BY-SA 4.0

name: Ringtail
fact: Was kept by miners as a mouser - the 'miner's cat' - though it's a raccoon relative.

name: Fisher
blurb: Species of small, carnivorous mammal native to North America
fact: One of the few predators that kills porcupines - it attacks the face, again and again, avoiding the quills.
credit: Mount Rainier National Park from Ashford, WA, United States · Public domain

name: Eurasian otter
fact: Its droppings, called spraint, are said to smell like jasmine tea.

name: North American river otter
fact: Slides down muddy and snowy banks on its belly, seemingly just for fun.

name: California sea lion
fact: A sea lion named Ronan learned to bob her head to the beat of music - the first non-human mammal shown to.
credit: (c) Jonathan Eisen, some rights reserved (CC BY) · CC BY 4.0

name: Roseate spoonbill
fact: Gets its pink from carotenoids in the crustaceans it sweeps up with its spoon-shaped beak.

name: Scarlet ibis
fact: Hatches dull brown and turns scarlet by eating red crustaceans.

name: Toco toucan
fact: Its giant beak is a radiator - it pumps blood into it to dump heat.

name: Rainbow lorikeet
fact: Has a brush-tipped tongue for mopping up nectar and pollen.

name: King penguin
fact: Has no nest - it carries its egg on its feet under a fold of warm belly skin.

name: Victoria crowned pigeon
fact: One of the largest pigeons on Earth, with a lace-like crown.

name: Hawksbill sea turtle
fact: Eats sponges full of glass-like spicules and toxins - and was filmed glowing red and green.

name: Blue tang
fact: Hides a scalpel-sharp spine by its tail.

name: Panther chameleon
fact: Changes colour by tuning tiny crystals in its skin, not by moving pigment.

name: Jackson's chameleon
fact: Males carry three horns and joust with them like tiny triceratopses.
credit: Movingsaletoday edited by Muhammad · Public domain

name: Crested gecko
fact: Was thought extinct until it was found again after a tropical storm in 1994.

name: Green tree python
fact: Born yellow or red, it turns green as it grows.

name: Strawberry poison dart frog
fact: The mother carries each tadpole up a tree to its own puddle in a plant, then feeds it unfertilised eggs.

stats.label: Babies
stats.value: Carried up trees one by one

name: Dyeing poison dart frog
fact: Legend says rubbing its toxins on a parrot made its feathers grow yellow.

name: Spiny leaf insect
blurb: Species of stick insect native to Australia
fact: Its eggs look like seeds, so ants carry them home - where they hatch safely.

name: Spiny orb-weaver
fact: Looks like a tiny spiky crab, and rebuilds its web every night, decorated with silk tufts that may warn birds away.
credit: Sam Fraser-Smith from Brisbane, Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Jaguarundi
fact: A long, low cat that looks more like an otter or weasel - and chirps like a bird.

name: Commerson's dolphin
fact: Often called the 'panda dolphin' for its black-and-white pattern.

stats.label: Colour
stats.value: Black and white like a panda

name: Common seadragon
fact: Males carry the eggs stuck to their tails until they hatch.

name: Zebra shark
fact: Striped as a baby and spotted as an adult - and females have had pups without a male.

name: Sally Lightfoot crab
fact: The 'Sally Lightfoot' crab dances across Galápagos rocks so nimbly it seems to skip over waves.

name: Harlequin shrimp
fact: Pairs flip starfish over and eat them alive, a tube foot at a time, over days.

name: Rüppell's vulture
fact: One was hit by a plane at 11,300 m over Côte d'Ivoire - the highest-flying bird ever recorded.

name: Resplendent quetzal
fact: Guatemala's currency is named after it - and it swallows wild avocados whole.

name: Bongo
fact: Licks burnt wood after lightning strikes, likely for the salts and minerals.
credit: Charles Miller from Basingstoke, United Kingdom · CC BY 2.0

name: Short-beaked echidna
blurb: Spiny furred egg-laying mammal from Australia
fact: A spiny mammal that lays eggs - its babies are called puggles.

name: Flat-headed cat
fact: Has webbed toes and backward-pointing teeth for catching slippery fish.

name: Irrawaddy dolphin
fact: Spits jets of water to herd fish - and in Myanmar used to cooperate with fishers.

name: Barreleye
fact: The 'barreleye' has a transparent head with green eyes that swivel inside it.

name: Atolla jellyfish
fact: The 'alarm jellyfish' flashes a spinning ring of blue lights when caught - a burglar alarm to bring bigger predators.
credit: NOAA Ocean Explorer from USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Pom-pom crab
fact: Waves tiny sea anemones in its claws like pom-poms to sting off attackers.

name: Lappet-faced vulture
fact: The most powerful African vulture - others wait for it to open a carcass.

name: Andean cock-of-the-rock
fact: Males gather and bob, squawk and bow together to show off to watching females.

name: Black-and-white ruffed lemur
fact: One of the loudest primates - and one of the few that parks its babies in a nest.

name: Golden lion tamarin
fact: Dads and older siblings do most of the baby-carrying.

name: Arabian oryx
fact: Was extinct in the wild, then brought back from zoo herds - the first animal ever moved from Extinct in the Wild to Vulnerable.

name: Addax
blurb: Species of antelope native to the Sahara
fact: Can go almost its whole life without drinking, getting water from plants.

name: Atlantic blue marlin
fact: Its stripes light up electric blue when it's hunting or excited.

name: Pteranodon
blurb: Genus of pterosaur of the Late Cretaceous
fact: Not a dinosaur - a flying reptile with a wingspan wider than a car.

name: Titanoboa
fact: The biggest snake ever found - longer than a bus and heavy as a small car.
credit: Nobu Tamura email:nobu.tamura@yahoo.com www.palaeocritti.com · CC BY 3.0

name: Dodo
fact: A giant flightless pigeon from Mauritius, gone within a century of humans arriving.

name: Raccoon
blurb: Medium-sized mammal native to North America
fact: About two-thirds of the touch-sensing part of its brain is devoted to its paws.

name: Sierra Nevada red fox
fact: Rediscovered near Sonora Pass in 2010 after decades without a confirmed sighting.

name: Carniolan honey bee
fact: Tells hive-mates where flowers are with a 'waggle dance' that encodes direction and distance.
credit: Richard Bartz, Munich Makro Freak & Beemaster Hubert Seibring, Munich which gave · CC BY-SA 2.5

name: Red-eyed tree frog
fact: Embryos can sense a snake shaking their egg clutch and hatch on the spot to escape.
credit: Red-eyed Tree Frog (Agalychnis callidryas) 3.jpg: Geoff Gallice from Gainesville · CC BY 2.0

name: Koala
blurb: Arboreal herbivorous marsupial native to Australia
fact: Has fingerprints so close to ours they could confuse a crime scene.

name: Giant Pacific octopus
fact: Has blue blood and can taste with its suckers.

name: Fennec fox
fact: The smallest canid - its giant ears dump heat and hear prey moving underground.

name: Virginia opossum
fact: 'Playing possum' is involuntary: it faints, drools and smells like death for up to hours.

stats.label: Teeth
stats.value: 50 - most of any N. American land mammal

name: American alligator
blurb: Crocodilian native to the Southeastern United States
fact: Has been around, nearly unchanged, for about 8 million years.

name: Axolotl
fact: Stays a larva its whole life, keeping its feathery gills forever.

name: Golden poison frog
fact: Its poison comes from its diet - captive-bred frogs fed crickets are harmless.

name: Satanic leaf-tailed gecko
blurb: Species of gecko endemic to Madagascar
fact: Looks so much like a dead leaf that it even has fake bite marks and decay on its tail.

name: Mandarinfish
fact: One of only two vertebrates known to make true blue pigment.

name: Philippine eagle
blurb: Endangered species of eagle in the Philippines
fact: Once called the 'monkey-eating eagle'; harming one in the Philippines can mean 12 years in jail.

name: Goblin shark
fact: Its jaws shoot forward like a slingshot to snatch prey.

name: Secretarybird
fact: Kills snakes by stomping them, with kicks faster than a blink.

name: Northern white rhinoceros
fact: Only two remain, Najin and Fatu, guarded around the clock in Kenya.

name: Amazon river dolphin
fact: Its unfused neck bones let it weave through flooded forests.

name: Giant squid
blurb: Deep-ocean dwelling squid in the family Architeuthidae
fact: Has the largest eyes of any animal (tied with the colossal squid).
credit: Natural History Museum of Denmark · CC BY 4.0

name: Sperm whale
fact: Makes the loudest sound of any animal.

name: King cobra
blurb: Group of venomous snakes from Asia
fact: The longest venomous snake - it hunts other snakes, cobras included.
credit: Michael Allen Smith from Seattle, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Bowhead whale
blurb: Baleen whale endemic to the Arctic
fact: The longest-lived mammal - one was found with a 19th-century harpoon point in it.
credit: Vicki Beaver, Alaska Fisheries Science Center, NOAA FIsheries, Marine Mammal Per · Public domain

name: Peregrine falcon
blurb: Fastest known animal and common bird of prey
fact: The fastest animal on Earth - in a hunting dive it moves faster than a Formula 1 car.

name: Peacock mantis shrimp
fact: Punches so fast the water boils into flashes of light, and it can break aquarium glass.

name: Thorny devil
fact: Drinks through its skin: grooves between its scales wick water to its mouth.

name: Leafy seadragon
fact: Disguised as floating seaweed - and, like seahorses, the males carry the eggs.

name: Bee hummingbird
fact: The smallest bird in the world - its nest is the size of a coin.

name: Giant golden-crowned flying fox
fact: One of the biggest bats in the world - and it only eats fruit.

name: Paradise flying snake
fact: Launches from trees, flattens its body and slithers through the air to glide.
credit: Alan Couch from Australia · CC BY 2.0

name: Sun bear
fact: Uses its huge tongue to slurp honey and insects out of tree holes.

name: Serval
fact: Leaps straight up to swat birds out of the air - one of the most successful cat hunters.

name: Pallas's cat
fact: Has the densest fur of any cat and an expression of permanent disappointment.
credit: Sander van der Wel · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Spectacled bear
fact: The only bear in South America - Paddington Bear came from "darkest Peru".

name: Pachycephalosaurus
fact: Its domed skull was up to 25 cm of solid bone - debate continues over whether it head-butted.

name: Humpback whale
fact: Males sing complex songs that spread from population to population like hit records.

name: Gaboon viper
fact: Has the longest fangs of any snake and the highest venom yield.

name: Reticulated python
fact: The longest snake in the world - it has turned up on remote islands after swimming.
credit: This photography was created by Mariluna. Other photos see here. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Maned wolf
fact: Looks like a fox on stilts - it isn't a wolf or a fox, and half its diet is fruit.

name: African wild dog
fact: Packs decide whether to go hunting by sneezing - enough sneezes and they go.

name: Bonobo
fact: Settles arguments through affection rather than fighting - and females run the group.

name: Bornean orangutan
fact: Builds a fresh nest in the trees every night - and sometimes uses a leaf as an umbrella.

name: Black-footed cat
blurb: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa
fact: One of Africa's smallest cats - and the most successful hunter of all cats.
credit: Patrick Ch. Apfeld, derivative editing by Poke2001 · CC BY 3.0

name: Portuguese man o' war
fact: Not a single animal but a colony of specialised individuals sailing together.
credit: Image courtesy of Islands in the Sea 2002, NOAA/OER. · Public domain

name: Vampire squid
fact: Neither a vampire nor a squid - it eats drifting debris and turns its cloak inside out when threatened.

name: Siberian musk deer
fact: Males have long fangs instead of antlers and use them to fight rivals.

name: Chimpanzee
fact: Some chimps make spears to hunt bushbabies - and crack nuts with stone hammers.

name: Stegosaurus stenops
blurb: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur
fact: Its tail spikes are officially nicknamed the 'thagomizer', after a Far Side cartoon.

name: Velociraptor mongoliensis
fact: The real one was turkey-sized and feathered - Jurassic Park's were based on Deinonychus.

name: Allosaurus
fact: May have attacked by slamming its open upper jaw down like a hatchet.

name: Carnotaurus
blurb: Genus of dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period
fact: Its name means 'meat-eating bull' - with bull horns and almost useless stub arms.
credit: Lida Xing and Yi Liu · CC BY 2.5

name: Mamenchisaurus
blurb: Sauropod dinosaur genus from Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous Period
fact: Its neck made up nearly half of its body length - one of the longest necks of any animal.
credit: The original uploader was ДиБгд at Russian Wikipedia. · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Black mamba
fact: One of the fastest snakes - named for the inky-black inside of its mouth, not its skin.

name: Green anaconda
fact: The heaviest snake in the world - it spends most of its time in water.

name: Colossal squid
fact: The heaviest invertebrate - with the biggest eyes of any known animal.
credit: This illustration was made by Citron You must credit this : Citron / CC-BY-SA-3. · CC BY 3.0

name: Tiger shark
fact: Called the "garbage can of the sea" - license plates and tyres have turned up in its stomach.

name: Whale shark
fact: The largest fish in the sea - every one has its own pattern of spots, like a fingerprint.

name: Nile crocodile
fact: A fearsome predator that gently carries its newly hatched babies in its jaws.

name: Spotted hyena
fact: Not a scavenger at heart - it kills most of its food and its laugh is a social signal.

name: Crowned eagle
fact: Africa's most powerful eagle - it takes monkeys and small antelope from the treetops.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Brachiosaurus
blurb: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period
fact: Stood like a giraffe, with longer front legs - its head reached a four-storey window.

name: Utahraptor
blurb: Genus of dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous
fact: The biggest raptor - a polar-bear-sized hunter with a 24 cm sickle claw.

name: Therizinosaurus
blurb: Dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous period
fact: Had the longest claws of any known animal - and probably used them to strip leaves.

name: Greenland shark
fact: The longest-lived vertebrate known - some alive today were born before the U.S. existed.

name: Harpy eagle
fact: Its talons are longer than a grizzly bear's claws.

name: Komodo dragon
fact: Females can reproduce without a male - virgin births have happened in zoos.

name: Honey badger
fact: Its loose skin lets it twist round and bite back while held - it eats venomous snakes.

name: Ankylosaurus
blurb: Ankylosaurid dinosaur genus from the Late Cretaceous Period
fact: Basically a living tank - its tail club could smash the leg bones of a predator.

name: Argentinosaurus
blurb: Extinct genus of giant sauropod dinosaur
fact: One of the heaviest land animals ever - a single vertebra is taller than a person.

stats.label: Record
stats.value: Among the biggest land animals ever

name: Coyote
blurb: Species of canine native to North America
fact: Has spread across almost all of North America - and now lives in Central Park and downtown Chicago.

name: Bat-eared fox
fact: Hears beetle larvae chewing underground with its giant ears.

name: Eurasian lynx
blurb: Species of medium-sized cat native to Eurasia
fact: Hunts deer several times its own size.

name: American black bear
fact: Can open car doors, jars and coolers with surprising skill.

name: Eyelash viper
fact: Has spiky scales over its eyes like eyelashes.
credit: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Goliath frog
fact: The biggest frog in the world - it moves rocks to build its own nursery pools.

name: Western barn owl
fact: Can catch a mouse in complete darkness by sound alone.

name: Asian water monitor
fact: The second-heaviest lizard, swimming between islands far out to sea.

name: Giraffe
fact: The tallest animal on Earth - its heart pumps blood two metres up to its brain.
credit: Muhammad Mahdi Karim Facebook The making of this document was supported by Wikim · GFDL 1.2

name: Gray wolf
fact: Yellowstone's wolves changed the course of rivers by controlling elk.

name: American bison
fact: Can sprint at 55 km/h and jump 2 metres high despite weighing a tonne.

name: Southern white rhinoceros
fact: Was down to fewer than 100 animals and is now the most numerous rhino.

name: Indian rhinoceros
fact: Its skin folds look like plates of armour.

name: Asian elephant
fact: Recognises itself in a mirror - one of very few animals that can.

name: African forest elephant
fact: Its seed-filled dung plants many of the trees in the Congo rainforest.

name: Western lowland gorilla
fact: Koko the gorilla learned to use about 1,000 signs.

name: Southeast African cheetah
fact: Accelerates faster than most sports cars.

name: Oceanic whitetip shark
fact: Jacques Cousteau called it the most dangerous of all sharks.
credit: Johan Lantz, Malmö SWEDEN · CC BY-SA 3.0

name: Coastal taipan
blurb: Venomous snake species native to Australia
fact: Strikes several times in an instant.
credit: Denise Chan from Hong Kong, China · CC BY-SA 2.0

name: Lion's mane jellyfish
